newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends weaker, regains some lost ground.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends weaker, regains some lost ground.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures clawed their way higher on Tuesday as light but persistent roaster buyers took advantage of the morning's weakness and so dragged nearbys off the earlier lows.
At one point, July eased $55 to set an intraday low of $2,045 but bargain-hunters were quick to moved in as the market paused after days of dizzy rallies.
Traders said the market was well covered into the afternoon, noting that the arabicas market also moved lower at the open on local and commission house selling.
"After the last few days it's no wonder it's paused to catch its breath," said one trader. "It looks like both markets are just consolidating."
Origin sellers were reported to be genreally absent.
At the close July was $25 lower at $2,075, with other nearbys down by around the same amount. Volume reached 5,822 lots.
Technically, July now looks to have started on a correction of its overbought condition as prices back off Monday's peak and new life-high of $2,190.
July's 14-day RSI (relative strength indicator), which stood at 86.1 at Monday's close, has edged lower to 81.7 but still remains heavily in overbought territory.
Short-term momentum indicators have also moved a touch lower after spending all of this month sloping higher in positive territory -- suggesting the market's upward trend could be slowing down.

Delegates at this week's meeting of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) said the grouping might favour a return to a trigger price mechanism to help regulate future supply to the market.
The draft proposal to be submitted to the ACPC council session on Wednesday envisaged retaining export quotas but with an emphasis on flexibility, they said.
